items.scene: at the door of a small restaurant or shop
items.note: 入って (haitte) is the て-form of 入ります (hairimasu, 'enter'). Add もいいですか (mo ii desu ka) to any て-form to ask 'may I ___?'.

items.scene: at a restaurant entrance
items.note: 予約 (yoyaku) is 'reservation'. ない (nai) is the plain 'there isn't' from あります (arimasu), so ないです (nai desu) is the polite 'I don't have'. Same shape as アレルギーはないです (arerugī wa nai desu, 'I don't have any allergies').
items.ttsText: よやくはないです
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.

items.target: パスポートをお願いします
items.scene: what staff ask at a hotel desk or a tax-free counter

items.english: Is this your first time in Japan?
items.scene: small talk with a stranger
items.note: 初めて (hajimete) is 'for the first time'. It is the same はじめ (hajime) as in はじめまして (hajimemashite, 'nice to meet you'), which literally means 'meeting for the first time'. Answer はい、初めてです (hai, hajimete desu, 'yes, it's my first time').

items.target: ご注文はお決まりですか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: 注文 (chūmon) is 'order', with ご (go) added for politeness. 決まり (kimari) comes from 決まります (kimarimasu, 'be decided'), with お (o) added. So it asks 'is your order decided?'. If you need longer: ちょっと待ってください (chotto matte kudasai, 'wait a moment, please').

items.target: アレルギーはありますか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: アレルギー (arerugī) is 'allergy', borrowed from German. ありますか (arimasu ka) is 'is there?' or 'do you have?'.

items.target: アレルギーはないです
items.note: ない (nai) is the plain negative of あります (arimasu, "there is").

items.english: Are there any foods you don't like?
items.target: 苦手な食べ物はありますか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: 食べ物 (tabemono, 'food') is 食べます (tabemasu, 'eat') without ます (masu), plus 物 (mono, 'thing'): an 'eat-thing'. お飲み物 (onomimono, 'drink') is built the same way. 苦手 (nigate) is something you don't get on with, softer than 'dislike', so this asks about dislikes, not allergies.

items.english: Is there anything you can't eat?
items.target: 食べられないものはありますか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: 食べられない (taberarenai, 'can't eat') is 食べ (tabe, from 食べます, tabemasu) plus られ (rare, 'can') plus ない (nai, 'not'). もの (mono) is 'thing'. It covers anything you can't eat for any reason, and is common before a set menu or a ryokan dinner.

何でも (nandemo, 'anything') is 何 (nan, 'what') plus でも (demo, 'even'). 食べられます (taberaremasu, 'can eat') is 食べます (tabemasu, 'eat') with られ (rare, 'can') added. A good answer to アレルギーはありますか (arerugī wa arimasu ka, 'Do you have any allergies?') and to 食べられないものはありますか (taberarenai mono wa arimasu ka, 'Is there anything you can't eat?').

items.english: Would you like something to drink?
items.target: お飲み物はいかがですか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: お飲み物 (onomimono, 'drink') is 飲み (nomi, from 飲みます, nomimasu, 'drink') plus 物 (mono, 'thing'), with a polite お (o) in front. いかがですか (ikaga desu ka) is 'how about?'.

items.english: What would you like to drink?
items.target: お飲み物は何になさいますか
items.scene: what a restaurant server asks
items.note: なさいます (nasaimasu) is the polite form of します (shimasu, 'do'), used by staff to customers. 何に (nani ni) is 'as what', so it literally asks 'what will you make your drink?'.

items.target: 店内でお召し上がりですか
items.scene: what a café or fast-food cashier asks
items.note: 店内 (tennai) is 'inside the shop': 店 (ten) is the kanji of 店 (mise, 'shop') and 内 (nai) is 'inside'. お召し上がり (omeshiagari) is the very polite way staff say 'eat'. Answer ここで食べます (koko de tabemasu, 'I'll eat here') or 持ち帰りでお願いします (mochikaeri de onegaishimasu, 'To take away, please').

items.scene: answering whether you're eating in or taking away
items.ttsText: ここでたべます
items.note: The answer to 店内でお召し上がりですか (tennai de omeshiagari desu ka, 'Will you be eating in?'). で (de) marks where you do something.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.

items.target: 持ち帰りでお願いします
items.scene: answering whether you're eating in or taking away
items.note: 持ち帰り (mochikaeri, 'takeaway') is 持ち (mochi, 'holding', as in 持ってきます, motte kimasu, 'bring') plus 帰り (kaeri, 'going home', from 帰ります, kaerimasu). Literally 'carrying it home'.

items.scene: what staff say at a restaurant entrance
items.note: 満席 (manseki, 'full') is 満 (man, 'full') plus 席 (seki, 'seat'): every seat is taken. ただいま (tadaima) here is a polite 'right now'.

items.scene: what staff say as you walk in
items.note: 好き (suki, 'like') with a polite お (o), plus 席 (seki, 'seat'). Literally 'please go to a seat you like'. へ (e) is 'to', like に (ni) for a direction.

items.scene: what an izakaya server says, putting down a small dish you didn't order
items.note: お通し (otōshi) is a small starter served at most izakaya. It is charged per person, usually ¥300 to ¥800, and it is normal to pay it.

items.target: お箸はおつけしますか
items.scene: what a konbini cashier asks
items.note: 箸 (hashi) is 'chopsticks', with a polite お (o). おつけします (otsuke shimasu) is a humble 'I'll include them', from つけます (tsukemasu, 'attach'). The cashier puts them in the bag if you say はい (hai, 'yes').

items.scene: what a konbini cashier asks about a bento or other ready meal
items.note: 温めます (atatamemasu) is 'heat up, warm'. Answer はい、お願いします (hai, onegaishimasu, 'yes, please') or いいえ、大丈夫です (iie, daijōbu desu, 'no, I'm fine').

items.target: これ、もう一つお願いします
items.note: もう一つ (mō hitotsu) is もう (mō, 'more') plus 一つ (hitotsu), the general counter for one item. It is the same もう as in もう一度 (mō ichido, 'one more time').

items.scene: what a cashier asks
items.note: お支払い (oshiharai, 'payment') comes from 支払います (shiharaimasu, 'pay'), with a polite お (o). The full question is お支払いはどうなさいますか (oshiharai wa dō nasaimasu ka, 'how would you like to pay?'). Answer カードでお願いします (kādo de onegaishimasu, 'By card, please').

items.target: カードを使ってもいいですか
items.scene: asking at the till before you order or buy
items.ttsText: カードをつかってもいいですか
items.note: 使って (tsukatte) is the て-form of 使います (tsukaimasu, 'use'). Add もいいですか (mo ii desu ka) to a て-form to ask 'may I ___?'.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.

items.target: カードでお願いします
items.scene: answering how you'll pay
items.note: で (de) marks how you pay. It is the same で as in 電車で行きます (densha de ikimasu, 'go by train').

items.scene: answering how you'll pay
items.note: 現金 (genkin) is 'cash'. で (de) marks how you pay, as in カードでお願いします (kādo de onegaishimasu, 'By card, please').

items.scene: a sign by a till or on a door
items.note: 現金 (genkin) is 'cash'. のみ (nomi) is a written word for 'only', used on signs.

items.scene: at the door of a shop or restaurant
items.note: やって (yatte) is the て-form of やります (yarimasu, 'do'), and います (imasu) makes it 'is doing'. So it asks 'are you doing business?'. It is the same やって as in どうやって (dō yatte, 'how').

items.scene: a sign on a shop or restaurant door
items.note: 営業 (eigyō) is 'doing business', and 中 (chū) is 'in the middle of'. So the sign says 'in business'.

items.scene: a sign on a shop or restaurant door
items.note: 準備 (junbi) is 'preparation', and 中 (chū) is 'in the middle of', the same 中 as on 営業中 (eigyōchū, 'Open'). Many restaurants hang it between lunch and dinner.

items.target: 以上でよろしいですか
items.scene: what a server or cashier asks after you order
items.note: 以上 (ijō) is 'that is all', said after a list. よろしい (yoroshii) is a polite いい (ii, 'good'). Answer はい (hai, 'yes').

items.scene: what a cashier asks
items.note: 袋 (fukuro) is 'bag'. 利用 (riyō) is a formal 'use', with a polite ご (go), so it asks 'will you use a bag?'. Bags cost a few yen, so you are always asked. Answer はい、お願いします (hai, onegaishimasu, 'yes, please') or いいえ、大丈夫です (iie, daijōbu desu, 'no, I'm fine').

items.scene: what someone says after you speak a little Japanese
items.ttsText: にほんごがじょうずですね
items.note: X が上手です (X ga jōzu desu) is 'is good at X', and ね (ne) makes it a friendly remark. In quick speech people often drop the が (ga).
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.

items.english: No, no, I've still got a long way to go.
items.target: いえいえ、まだまだです
items.scene: replying when someone praises your Japanese
items.note: The modest, expected reply. まだ (mada) is 'still, not yet', and doubled, まだまだ (mada mada) is 'still a long way off'. Saying ありがとうございます (arigatō gozaimasu, 'thank you') on its own can sound like you agree you are good.

items.target: 日本語は少しわかります
items.note: A good opener before you ask something, so people know to keep it simple.
items.ttsText: にほんごはすこしわかります
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.

items.target: ゆっくりお願いします
items.note: ゆっくり (yukkuri) is 'slowly, at ease'. You will also hear ごゆっくりどうぞ (goyukkuri dōzo, 'take your time').

items.scene: what staff say when they take your order or request
items.note: A very polite 'understood', used by staff to customers. It means the same as わかりました (wakarimashita, 'understood'), but humbler.

items.target: 試着してもいいですか
items.scene: in a clothes shop
items.note: 試着 (shichaku) is 試 (shi, 'try') plus 着 (chaku, 'wear'): 'try-wear'. 試着します (shichaku shimasu) is 'try on', and して (shite) is the て-form of します (shimasu). Then もいいですか (mo ii desu ka, 'may I?'), as in 入ってもいいですか (haitte mo ii desu ka, 'May I come in?').
An adjective, not a verb, so the thing you want takes が (ga), not を (o): これが欲しいです (kore ga hoshii desu, 'I want this'). Often written in kana, ほしい. For wanting to DO something, use たい (tai).
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: ほしい

items.note: Attaches to a verb's ます-stem: 買います (kaimasu, 'buy') becomes 買いたいです (kaitai desu, 'I want to buy'), and 行きます (ikimasu, 'go') becomes 行きたいです (ikitai desu, 'I want to go'). It changes like an い-adjective, so 'don't want to' is たくないです (takunai desu).
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.

items.scene: pointing at something in a shop
items.note: This says you want it. To ask staff to give it to you, これをください (kore o kudasai, 'this, please') is the request.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: これがほしいです

items.scene: a friend asking, say about a present
items.note: Fine with friends. Asking a stranger outright what they want sounds blunt, so shop staff say 何かお探しですか (nanika osagashi desu ka, 'Are you looking for something?') instead.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: なにがほしいですか

items.target: もっと安いのが欲しいです
items.scene: in a shop, after hearing the price
items.note: の (no) stands in for the thing, like 'one' in 'a cheaper one'. もっと (motto) is 'more' and 安い (yasui) is 'cheap'.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: もっとやすいのがほしいです

items.note: 買いたい (kaitai, 'want to buy') is 買います (kaimasu, 'buy') plus たい (tai). With たい the thing can take を (o) or が (ga); を is more common in speech. With 欲しい (hoshii) it is always が.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: これをかいたいです

items.english: I want to buy a ticket.
items.target: チケットを買いたいです
items.scene: at a train station
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.
items.ttsText: チケットをかいたいです
items.note: 買いたい (kaitai, 'want to buy') is 買います (kaimasu, 'buy') with ます (masu) swapped for たい (tai). Station machines and signs say 切符 (kippu) for a train ticket, and staff understand either word.

items.target: これはどうやって買いますか
items.scene: at a ticket machine or vending machine
items.note: どうやって (dō yatte) asks how to do something, and 買います (kaimasu) is 'buy'. The same question works with any verb: これはどうやって使いますか (kore wa dō yatte tsukaimasu ka, 'How do I use this?').
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: これはどうやってかいますか

items.english: I want this, but how do I buy it?
items.target: これが欲しいんですが、どうやって買いますか
items.scene: asking a passer-by or staff for help at a machine
items.note: んですが (n desu ga) softens what you just said and leads into the question, the usual polite way to ask for help. どうやって買いますか (dō yatte kaimasu ka) is 'how do I buy it?'.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: これがほしいんですが、どうやってかいますか

items.target: これはどうやって使いますか
items.note: Same shape as これはどうやって買いますか (kore wa dō yatte kaimasu ka, 'How do I buy this?'), with 使います (tsukaimasu, 'use') in place of 買います (kaimasu, 'buy').
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.
items.ttsText: これはどうやってつかいますか
items.scene: stuck at a ticket machine or a vending machine

items.english: Please show me how to use it.
items.target: 使い方を教えてください
items.note: 使い方 (tsukaikata) is 'how to use'. 教えて (oshiete) is the て-form of 教えます (oshiemasu, 'teach, tell'), and て-form plus ください (kudasai) is 'please do'.
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: つかいかたをおしえてください

items.english: I want to go here, but how do I get there?
items.target: ここに行きたいんですが、どうやって行きますか
items.scene: showing someone a map on your phone
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: ここにいきたいんですが、どうやっていきますか
items.note: 行きたい (ikitai, 'want to go') is 行きます (ikimasu, 'go') plus たい (tai). どうやって行きますか (dō yatte ikimasu ka) is 'how do I get there?'.

items.english: What do you want to eat?
items.scene: a friend asking
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.
items.ttsText: なにをたべたいですか
items.note: 食べたい (tabetai, 'want to eat') is 食べます (tabemasu, 'eat') with ます (masu) swapped for たい (tai).

items.scene: showing a shop assistant a photo on your phone
items.note: 探しています (sagashite imasu, 'am looking for') is 探して (sagashite), the て-form of 探します (sagashimasu, 'look for'), plus います (imasu), which makes it '-ing'. Staff will often ask first: 何かお探しですか (nanika osagashi desu ka, 'Are you looking for something?').
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: cover wanting a thing (ほしい) and wanting to do (たい), plus asking how to buy or use something.
items.ttsText: これをさがしています

items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: the deck used 現金 in three cards but had no card for the word itself.
items.ttsText: げんきん
items.note: 現 (gen) is 'present, actual', and 金 (kin) is the kanji in お金 (okane, 'money').

items.english: Please show me how to buy a ticket.
items.target: チケットの買い方を教えてください
items.scene: at a station ticket machine or window
items.note: 買い方 (kaikata, 'how to buy') is 買います (kaimasu, 'buy') without ます (masu), plus 方 (kata, 'way'). The same shape gives 使い方 (tsukaikata, 'how to use').
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-06: reworded to vocabulary and patterns the owner has already studied, so the card is easier to learn.
items.ttsText: チケットのかいかたをおしえてください

items.note: 買えます (kaemasu, 'can buy') is 買います (kaimasu, 'buy') with the い (i) before ます (masu) changed to え (e). That works for many verbs: 使います (tsukaimasu, 'use') becomes 使えます (tsukaemasu, 'can use'). で (de) marks the place where the buying happens.
items.ttsText: どこでかえますか
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: two shop phrases added alongside the wanting batch.

items.scene: replying when shop staff ask if you need help
items.note: 見て (mite) is the て-form of 見ます (mimasu, 'look'), and adding いる (iru) makes it '-ing'. だけ (dake) is 'just, only'. A polite answer to 何かお探しですか (nanika osagashi desu ka, 'Are you looking for something?').
items.ttsText: みているだけです
items.reviewNote: Owner request 2026-11-04: two shop phrases added alongside the wanting batch.
